newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Bertinotti more optimistic on mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Bertinotti more optimistic on mini-budget.

text.p: Fausto Bertinotti, leader of Italy's hard-left Communist Refoundation party, said on Friday that progress had been made over a planned mini-budget and he was now less pessimistic about its chances.
He said that an agreement hammered out between the centre-left government and its allies on measures to counter unemployment had improved the mini-budget's prospects.
"If I had to make a prediction (on the mini-budget) before this (employment agreement), I would have been pessimistic. Then we took a step forward," he told a news conference.
Bertinotti said on Thursday that the deal, reached after a four-hour meeting, meant that 100,000 jobs would be created for young people in the underdeveloped south.
However Bertinotti said on Friday that the mini-budget still faced a difficult passage through parliament.
"I don't want to spread false optimism. I say it will be a difficult passage. The whole country needs to help this government avoid false steps," he said.
Bertinotti said Refoundation still believed the mini-budget was not necessary but it was open to dialogue, although it would not tolerate spending cuts or new taxes.

Refoundation, which remains outside the centre-left coalition, holds the balance of power in the lower house of parliament and has said repeatedly it will block any cuts in welfare spending or fresh tax hikes.
Bertinotti said Prime Minister Romano Prodi would consult all the parties in the coalition and Refoundation on the mini-budget over the coming weeks.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has indicated the package, due by the end of April, will raise around 14 trillion lire ($8.3 billion) in a bid to reduce the country's deficit to three percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to make the grade for early entry into the single European currency.
